extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, researchers, and policymakers interested in nuclear accidents and safety
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive encyclopedic article describing the March 28, 1979 Three Mile Island nuclear accident: its causes, timeline, regulatory responses, investigations, health and environmental monitoring, cleanup, and industry effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: INES classification
rubrics_metrics.description: On the seven-point logarithmic International Nuclear Event Scale, the TMI-2 reactor accident is rated Level 5, an "Accident with Wider Consequences".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article uses the INES as a metric to classify the severity of the event; Level 5 denotes an accident with wider consequences on that scale and provides a standardized severity label.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC shutdown rule for auxiliary feed pumps
rubrics_metrics.description: The closure of these valves was a violation of a key Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) rule, according to which the reactor must be shut down if all auxiliary feed pumps are closed for maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit regulatory requirement cited as a failure mode in the narrative; compliance with such NRC rules is presented as a safety criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of control-room indicators (valve position)
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no direct indication of the valve's actual position. A light labelled 'Light on - RC-RV2 open' indicated that the PORV pilot valve's solenoid was powered, not the actual status of the PORV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrumentation in the control room should indicate actual equipment status (e.g., valve position) rather than proxy signals (solenoid power). The article treats lack of direct indication as a design flaw that contributed to misdiagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety-grade indicator suite completeness and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A downstream temperature indicator ... was not part of the 'safety grade' suite of indicators designed to be used after an incident, and its location behind the seven-foot-high instrument panel meant that it was effectively out of sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety-grade indicators should include relevant sensors (e.g., downstream temperature) and be located/arranged for ready visibility and use during incidents; omission or poor placement is critiqued as reducing situational awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator training for ambiguous indicators and uncommon symptom combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The operators had not been trained to understand the ambiguous nature of the PORV indicator and to look for alternative confirmation that the main relief valve was closed. Operators' training and plant procedures did not cover a situation where the two parameters went in opposite directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training programs should cover ambiguous instrument indications, alternative confirmation methods, and atypical parameter behavior (e.g., pressurizer level and RCS pressure moving opposite), because lack of such training contributed to failure to recognize the LOCA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures covering pressurizer/pressure behavior during LOCA
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected symptoms for a LOCA were drops in both RCS pressure and pressurizer level. The water level in the pressurizer was rising because ... This mechanism had not been trained. Indications of high water levels in the pressurizer contributed to confusion ... and led operators to turn off the emergency core cooling pumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational procedures should explicitly address the specific thermodynamic mechanisms that can produce counterintuitive readings (e.g., pressurizer level rise with falling pressure during PORV leakage) and prescribe correct responses (e.g., preserving emergency core cooling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and correct use of emergency core cooling systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators turned off the emergency core cooling pumps ... due to fears the system was being overfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency core cooling pumps, which start automatically during coolant loss events, should be maintained and not be shut off inappropriately; proper procedures and training should prevent disabling emergency cooling due to misinterpretation of indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency response organizational readiness and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC faced the same problems in obtaining accurate information as the state and was further hampered by being organizationally ill-prepared to deal with emergencies, as it lacked a clear command structure and did not have the authority either to tell the utility what to do or to order an evacuation of the local area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency response organizations must have a clear command structure, lines of authority, and the ability to direct utilities and order public-protective actions (e.g., evacuations) during crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evacuation advisory criteria for vulnerable populations
rubrics_metrics.description: I am advising those who may be particularly susceptible to the effects of any radiation, that is, pregnant women and pre-school aged children, to leave the area within a five-mile radius of the Three Mile Island facility until further notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article records evacuation guidance targeted to vulnerable groups (pregnant women, pre-school children) within a specified radius (initially five miles), and later notes extension of evacuation zones (to 20 miles). Such advisories are presented as pragmatic protective-action criteria used during the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental monitoring and sampling protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Within hours of the accident, the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) began daily sampling of the environment at the three stations closest to the plant. Continuous monitoring at 11 stations was established on April 1 and was expanded to 31 stations on April 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-release environmental monitoring should include rapid deployment of sampling, expansion to continuous monitoring and multiple stations to characterize contamination and exposure; the article uses the EPA response to exemplify monitoring practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate, timely communication to authorities and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: The uncertainty of operators at the plant was reflected in fragmentary, ambiguous, or contradictory statements made by Met Ed to government agencies and to the press, particularly about the possibility and severity of off-site radioactivity releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilities and response agencies are expected to provide clear, accurate, and timely information to regulators, officials, and the public; contradictory or downplaying statements are identified as worsening public distrust and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance, maintenance, and equipment reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation strongly criticized Babcock & Wilcox, Met Ed, General Public Utilities, and the NRC for lapses in quality assurance and maintenance ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust quality assurance and maintenance programs are required to prevent equipment failures and ensure reliable operation; lapses are treated as systemic contributors to accidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer/customer notification of recurring component failures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kemeny Commission noted that Babcock & Wilcox's PORV had previously failed on 11 occasions ... Although Babcock engineers recognized the problem, the company failed to clearly notify its customers of the valve issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers are expected to notify customers and affected operators of recurring component failures and systemic problems so corrective actions and mitigations can be implemented at user sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational and procedural reforms recommended after major incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: "... fundamental changes will be necessary in the organization, procedures, and practices—and above all—in the attitudes" of the NRC and the nuclear industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-incident recommendations include comprehensive reforms to organization, procedures, practices, and culture (attitudes) within regulators and industry to reduce complacency and improve safety; the Kemeny Commission frames these as necessary corrective standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-accident cleanup standard: public health protection and containment
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1988, the NRC announced that, although it was possible to further decontaminate the Unit 2 site, the remaining radioactivity had been sufficiently contained as to pose no threat to public health and safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on decontamination are framed in terms of whether remaining radioactivity poses a threat to public health and safety; containment to acceptable public-health thresholds is used as a criterion for concluding major cleanup phases.
